newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China Nov/Dec diesel imports up about 20 percent.
newsitem.headline: China Nov/Dec diesel imports up about 20 percent.

text.p: China has raised its November and December diesel imports by almost 20 percent over the monthly volumes seen in the past few months due to reduced crude runs at inland refineries, industry sources said on Thursday.
Traders said China raised its November and December diesel imports by least 100,000 tonnes for a total of about 600,000 tonnes for each month.
"Since around September, refineries in China have cut output by between 10 and 20 percent due to high crude oil prices," a source at state-refiner SINOPEC told Reuters.
The SINOPEC source said Chinese refiners had not raised their crude oil imports substantially and output would be raised only marginally in January.
Sinopec owns a majority of China's refining capacity with a total refining ouput of about 4.1 million barrels per day.
As a result of China's recent purchases, diesel prices in Singapore have soared to new five-year highs.

On Wednesday, one trader in Singapore was bidding for a second half December cargo at $32.60 per barrel on a free-on-board (fob) basis, up sharply from the five-year record trade of $31.80 a barrel chalked up a week ago.
In addition to reduced crude runs, the higher Chinese imports were also due to peak winter demand prior to the Lunar New Year holidays in early February.
"China is buying ahead of the Lunar New Year holidays," one trader said. The Chinese market is usually closed for one to two weeks for the holidays," he said.
Traders said China's imports for January were likely to hover around the 600,000-tonne mark rather than the usual 500,000 tonnes.

China has also been paying record levels for diesel imports with the most recent cargo bought at $252 a tonne on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to southern China. This was about $20 a tonne over purchase levels made for December delivery about two week ago.
Small barge lots of between 1,000-3,000 tonnes each were sold earlier on Thursday at $265 per tonne on an ex-terminal basis from Hong Kong for shipment to southern China, traders said.
